must_fix: C005 (confirmed, mechanical): 'ip status' (SKILL.md:294) offers the value 'substituted', but the only assignment rule given (SKILL.md:308-310) defines 'cleared' and 'not-yet-cleared' only -- no step ever tells the reader to assign 'substituted'. Note step 7 already has a separate 'substituted' field (SKILL.md:295) for the same information, making it unclear the ip-status value is even a coherent third state.

Steps 6-7 narrate file mutation (remove an option, replace a block with a stub, shrink source text, substitute a stand-in matching shape) as bare agent actions with no handoff wrapping the mutation itself -- only the subsequent rebuild is handed off (SKILL.md:223-244). Since allowed-tools is Read, Grep, Glob only, the agent cannot perform any of these edits, and the skill never discloses this limitation the way it discloses 'cannot build or run.' Fix: reframe each axis as a proposal ('propose removing X') and add an explicit 'ask the engineer to make this cut' handoff before the existing rebuild handoff, mirroring dv-minimal-reproducer's step 4 phrasing.

Step 6's requirement to 'compare the signature against step 4's yourself' after every cut has zero allocated Grep/Read budget in a skill whose retrieval budget is stated as a single closed pool already spent by steps 1-5 (SKILL.md:96-105, 233-234). Fix: add a per-cut budget allowance, matching dv-minimal-reproducer/SKILL.md:79-85's explicit per-iteration model.

Same failure pattern as C005 on a second field: 'class : design | infrastructure | unknown' (SKILL.md:290) is only ever explained for 'design' and 'infrastructure' (SKILL.md:305-309, plus a generic 'leave empty rather than fill plausibly'); no step ever tells the reader to assign 'unknown'.
technical_errors: Step 6's axis-skip rule (SKILL.md:223-224) says a compile/elaboration defect should 'skip straight to 3' (Hierarchy), which skips both axis 1 (Time/stimulus, correctly -- no run occurred) and axis 2 (Options). But the skill's own Gotcha (SKILL.md:333-335) says defects that 'fire only under a particular optimisation, incremental-compile or debug setting' are common -- exactly a compile/elab-time Options concern -- so skipping Options reduction for this defect class looks inconsistent with its own Gotcha. Disposition table row 3 (SKILL.md:168, 'An option in the step 2 invocation selects exactly this behaviour | not ours | back to dv-customer-escalation-isolation') doesn't follow the 'disposition: X' format every other row uses, nor does it say 'leave the disposition empty' the way the last row does -- leaves ambiguous whether/how this skill's own record is populated before handing off. Confidence ~55.
verb_honesty: Step 6 bullet 1 (SKILL.md:223): "Stop the run just after the failure point." — bare imperative; agent cannot run anything.
Step 6 bullet 2 (SKILL.md:225): "Remove one option at a time from the step 2 set." — bare file-edit verb, no handoff attached to the removal itself.
Step 6 bullet 3 (SKILL.md:228): "Replace blocks the failure never reaches with stubs carrying the same port list" — bare file-write verb.
Step 6 bullet 5 (SKILL.md:231): "Unreferenced declarations first, then shrink what survives." — bare edit verb.
Step 7 (SKILL.md:243): "take the stand-in from the Substitution library slot and match the shape, not the contents" — bare verb describing creating/swapping a file.

Step 6's only handoff (SKILL.md:233-235) covers 'ask the engineer to rebuild the reduced tree' — this presupposes the cut already exists; it never hands off the act of making the cut. Contrast with dv-minimal-reproducer/SKILL.md:177-178, which this step explicitly says to 'use as written': 'Propose exactly one change... Then ask the engineer to make that one change, run it, and give you the path of the resulting log.' dv-tool-bug-testcase-extraction never adopts that propose/ask-engineer framing.

Intro 'What this does not do' (SKILL.md:30-33) lists compile/elaborate/start-tool/compare-runs as things the agent cannot do, but never discloses that it also cannot write or edit files (allowed-tools is Read, Grep, Glob only) -- a material omission given steps 6-8 are almost entirely file mutation.
hallucination_risks: Low overall -- no invented tool flags, message strings, or proprietary conventions found; the author consistently routed team-specific facts through [[FILL:]] slots or the shared profile.

Minor/soft: 'the applications engineer' (SKILL.md:145) is asserted as a known handoff recipient without appearing in any 'Who knows' column of the slot table; plausible as generic EDA-industry terminology rather than an invented house convention, so flagged only at low confidence (~50).
budget_violations: Retrieval budget (SKILL.md:96-105) is a single closed pool of 3 Glob / 5 Grep / 4 Read, entirely attributed to steps 2, 3, 4 and 5 by its own accounting. Step 6 nonetheless assigns the agent recurring work requiring fresh Grep/Read: 'ask the engineer to rebuild the reduced tree and give you the path of the resulting log, then compare the signature against step 4's yourself' (SKILL.md:233-234) -- this must happen after every cut across five axes, and none of that Grep/Read is budgeted anywhere.

This is a confirmed gap relative to the sibling skill this step cites: dv-minimal-reproducer/SKILL.md:79-85 explicitly defines a per-iteration budget ('one Grep for the fatal markers... at most two Read windows... Three named Grep groups sit outside that per-iteration budget') because every shrink cycle produces a new log to re-examine. dv-tool-bug-testcase-extraction has no equivalent per-iteration allowance, so step 6 as written cannot be carried out inside the skill's own stated caps.

Step 8's closing handoff ('ask the engineer to build the packaged testcase... and to give you the log path,' SKILL.md:275-277) implies a final signature check against step 4's result (per 'Done when,' SKILL.md:374-375) that likewise requires an unbudgeted Grep/Read of that final log.
review.open_twice: "Partially. Steps 1-5 (the confirmation gate) are tight, honestly bounded, and would likely earn repeat trust on their own. But an engineer following through to step 6 will hit two compounding problems on first real use: it's unclear who performs the actual cut (remove/replace/shrink), and the repeated signature-verification work has no budget once the fixed Grep/Read pool from steps 1-5 is spent. A senior engineer doing a full extraction end-to-end would likely notice this on the first pass and stop trusting steps 6-8 -- the exact shelfware failure mode the pack's verb-honesty rule targets."

recheck.why: Lint is 1.000 and clean, metadata role/level are exactly eda-product-validation-engineer/intermediate, the DV content is technically correct throughout (finalise-vs-post, compile-time option axis, stub shape-dependence, protected regions, LRM latitude), all eight slots are spent, and the fixed pool reconciles exactly against every step. But two defects bite in the first hour of a real case. (a) Budget rule 6's 200-hit ceiling forbids the one Grep step 5 must make — the whole-tree ownership-header sweep whose hit count scales with tree size — and neither remedy it offers works, so the Grep that gates ip status has no legal way to run; the sibling dv-artifact-redaction-egress already solves this with a spare Grep and a 'pervasive' outcome. (b) The block spells the R&D routing line as the bare locked noun `owner`, which _shared/handoff-vocabulary.md reserves as a T3 shape for the profile's area-to-owner map, and which dv-customer-defect-handoff — the skill this one hands its record to — explicitly renamed to `route owner` for this exact question, writing down why. It also has no slot and no step behind it. I cannot distinguish new regressions from pre-existing issues without lineage, so all findings are listed under remaining; the two that visibly contradict a fix already applied elsewhere in the pack are also flagged as new_problems.
remaining: BLOCKER — budget rule 6 forbids step 5's required Grep. Rule 6 (line 118): 'Any Grep returning more than about 200 hits is too broad. Anchor it on the diagnostic identifier or on one directory before opening anything.' Step 5 (line 225): 'Grep across the tree for the ownership header words the Retention rule slot names', then 'Classify every path into exactly one class.' Copyright/proprietary header words hit essentially every source file, so the count scales with tree size and exceeds 200 on any real customer submission. Neither remedy works: anchoring on the diagnostic identifier finds no headers, and anchoring on one directory contradicts 'classify every path' and forces ip status: not-yet-cleared by construction. This is the Grep that gates ip status — the field deciding whether anything of theirs may be kept. Fix: give rule 6 an explicit exception for the inventory Grep (hit count is proportional to files, which is the point), or adopt the shape the routing partner dv-artifact-redaction-egress already uses at its lines 78-84 — one spare Grep to re-narrow once, and a defined outcome when a class is still that broad.

BLOCKER — `owner` (line 349) reuses a locked shape name for a different question, with no slot and no step. _shared/handoff-vocabulary.md T3 registers `owner` as shape: 'The name from the profile's area-to-owner map, or blank plus candidates', and 'the spelling is locked, there is no enum, and the name may not be reused for anything else.' This skill writes `owner : <the R and D component this routes to, or blank plus candidates>`. dv-customer-defect-handoff asks the identical question and deliberately does NOT use the bare noun — its line 240 is `route owner : <the R&D queue or component owner this routes to, per the Escalation route slot>`, and its line 249 says why: 'The routing line is `route owner`, not the bare noun: the pack's field registry locks that spelling to the profile's area-to-owner map... Two records pasted into one table must never put two questions under one label.' The other routing partner dv-customer-escalation-isolation line 269 spells `owner` the registered way. Since step 3 hands the record to defect-handoff and step 9 claims the records 'read side by side and a case moves between them without translation', the mis-join is live. Fix: rename to `route owner`.

BLOCKER (same field, second half) — nothing assigns `owner`. No [[FILL:]] slot supplies the R&D component route (dv-customer-defect-handoff carries an 'Escalation route' slot at its line 58 for exactly this), no numbered step derives it — the only support is two incidental clauses inside step 4 (line 203 'they route to different R and D components'; line 218 '`where` is what routes the case to an R&D component') — and the Human-verification list never checks it. The skill carefully disambiguates five other profile facts (Log location, Pass marker, Fatal markers, Bug convention, Simulator) but never mentions Area to owner map, the one it is actually shadowing. Fix: add the routing slot and a step that assigns it, or drop the field entirely and let dv-customer-defect-handoff own routing — step 3 already says that skill owns the record.

MEDIUM — `disposition`'s registered meaning contradicts the field. _shared/handoff-vocabulary.md line 116 records the held noun as 'What the vendor did with the extracted testcase', and dv-coverage-hole-disposition line 288-289 repeats that wording when telling readers the name was unavailable to it. The actual field (line 338) is the pre-carving gate verdict `defect | documented-limitation | fixed-in-later-release | doc-gap | enhancement`, decided in step 3 before any testcase exists ('Carving starts only on disposition: defect'), and in this skill we ARE the vendor (role eda-product-validation-engineer), so the note's frame is wrong twice over. Holder registration is correct so the checker passes, but two pack files now describe this field wrongly. Fix the registry note and the sibling's prose, or rename the field.

MINOR — `residual` is thinly assigned. `residual : <anything of theirs still in the tree, and who holds the ruling>` is supported only obliquely by step 5's classification plus the Retention rule slot's ruling owner and one clause of step 9 prose. No step instructs the reader to enumerate what of theirs is still in the tree. Every other block value has a clear assigning step.

MINOR — budget rule 2 vs step 4 precondition. Rule 2 says the single 60-line window into their design source is opened 'at a line a Grep already returned', but step 4 takes the line from the diagnostic text inside the 80-line log Read window. It is defensible (the diagnostic came from Grep #2's hit and its text names file and line), but it reads as a mismatch on first pass. Say 'at the file and line the step 3 diagnostic names'.

MINOR — step 2's handoff over-identifies a person: 'ask the support lead who owns this case — the same person the Case tree and Case record slots name'. Those slots' Who-knows column names the role 'support lead' twice; it does not establish that one named person owns this case, the unpack area and the record convention. Rule 8 territory, soft because the role string genuinely is identical.

OBSERVATION — length is 442 lines against the brief's stated 180-260. The pack norm has drifted (dv-minimal-reproducer 448, dv-compute-license-efficiency 456, dv-cross-tool-mismatch-adjudication 442) and the lint does not gate it, so this is a pack-wide question rather than this file's alone — but the file sits at the very top of the distribution and step 9's three prose paragraphs after the fenced block are the most compressible text in it.

OBSERVATION — the `public` class ('the language standard's own packages, freely redistributable models', marked keep) is close to a null category for a SystemVerilog carve: the standard's own packages are built into the simulator and are never copied into the carved tree at all. Not wrong, but it earns less than the other four rows.
new_problems: `owner` at line 349 uses the bare T3 shape noun for the R&D component route — the exact question dv-customer-defect-handoff renamed to `route owner`, with its rationale written into its own body at line 249. The fix was applied to the sibling and not to this file, and the two skills route records to each other.

The `disposition` field's meaning has drifted away from what _shared/handoff-vocabulary.md line 116 and dv-coverage-hole-disposition line 288 both record for it ('what the vendor did with the extracted testcase'); it is now the pre-carving gate verdict set in step 3.
